finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a fully attacker-supplied URL. The host check at line 13 uses an unanchored suffix match with no label boundary, so attacker-registered domains such as attackerexample.com pass. Nothing blocks private, loopback, or link-local IPs, so the server can be pointed at internal services and cloud metadata.

trace.note: `url` comes straight from the query string.
`urlparse(url).hostname` extracts the host for the check.

`host.endswith("example.com")` also matches `attackerexample.com`, `evilexample.com`, and similar. There is no leading dot. The unused constant `ALLOWED_SUFFIX = ".example.com"` at line 7 suggests the dot was intended.
Default httpx client, with no transport, dialer, or IP filter.
The original raw string is passed to httpx, which re-parses it. The DNS name is resolved at connect time, so attacker DNS can return 127.0.0.1, 10.x, or 169.254.169.254.
Response size `len(r.text)` is returned, which is a length oracle on the internal response.

finding.guards_checked: Host check (line 13): urlparse hostname then endswith, bypassable by any domain ending in example.com without a dot. Scheme: not checked by the app, but httpx only speaks http and https, so file: and gopher: are unreachable. Redirects: httpx defaults to follow_redirects=False, so not a finding on its own. IP/private-range blocking: absent. DNS pinning or connect-time address check: absent (case 12 pattern). Port restriction: absent. Parser differential (urlparse vs httpx): not separately exploited; the suffix bypass is sufficient. /ping (line 23): hardcoded URL, ruled out.
finding.repro: GET /mirror?url=http://attackerexample.com:8080/admin where attackerexample.com resolves to 127.0.0.1 (attacker-controlled DNS). Or http://attackerexample.com/latest/meta-data/ with DNS pointing at 169.254.169.254. Conditional: internal-only hostnames under example.com (split-horizon DNS, e.g. intranet.example.com resolving to a private IP) are reachable without attacker DNS.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is mirror.py:13, `host.endswith("example.com")`, which is the unanchored suffix match the candidate describes, so it does not close the finding. No IP/private-range filter, port restriction, or DNS pinning exists anywhere in mirror.py. The /ping route at mirror.py:23 uses a hardcoded URL and is not a source.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) is unauthenticated attacker input, and mirror.py:13 `endswith("example.com")` accepts hosts like attackerexample.com, which then reach the unfiltered `httpx.AsyncClient().get(url)` at mirror.py:16, so the trace holds and the SSRF is not closed by any guard.
